equation_request.abstract:
We discuss decoherence in discrete-time quantum walks in terms of a phenomenological model that distinguishes spin and spatial decoherence. We identify the dominating mechanisms that affect quantum walk experiments realized with neutral atoms walking in an optical lattice.

From the measured spatial distributions, we determine with good precision the amount of decoherence per step, which provides a quantitative indication of the quality of our quantum walks. In particular, we find that spin decoherence is the main mechanism responsible for the loss of coherence in our experiment. We also find that the sole observation of ballistic instead of diffusive expansion in position space is not a good indicator for the range of coherent delocalization.

We provide further physical insight by distinguishing the effects of short and long time spin dephasing mechanisms. We introduce the concept of coherence length in the discrete-time quantum walk, which quantifies the range of spatial coherences. Unexpectedly, we find that quasi-stationary dephasing does not modify the local properties of the quantum walk, but instead affects spatial coherences.

For a visual representation of decoherence phenomena in phase space, we have developed a formalism based on a discrete analogue of the Wigner function. We show that the effects of spin and spatial decoherence differ dramatically in momentum space.

specification.problem: Model a discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW) of a spin-1/2 coin on a small cyclic lattice with spin dephasing and spatial dephasing, and read out position distribution, spatial coherence length from rho(x,x'), and a discrete Wigner function. The abstract gives no formulas; this is a phenomenological model reconstruction.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One instance: n=3 position qubits (8 sites, assumed; n=4 is possible if the cap allows), 1 coin qubit, fresh ancillas per step for T<=3 steps (or averaging over sampled random-phase circuits). Computes P(x,t), a coherence length from the reduced density matrix, and a discrete Wigner function classically. Outside scope: fitting to the neutral-atom experiment, the distinction between short- and long-time dephasing as tied to real experimental noise, and the paper's exact Wigner formalism and decoherence parametrization.

symbols.meaning: spatial dephasing probability per step (damping of |x><x'| coherence)
position reduced density matrix (coin traced out)
coherence profile, sum over x of |rho(x,x+d)|

symbols.domain: real, x in Z_N, k in Z_N

symbols.meaning: fixed Z angle on the spin per run for quasi-stationary dephasing
symbols.domain: random real, e.g. Gaussian, constant over steps

equations.label: Step operator
equations.description: Hadamard coin followed by a spin-conditional shift on a cyclic lattice (increment for spin 0, decrement for spin 1); the lattice index is read as an integer from the position qubits, with the least significant bit as qubit 0.
equations.justification: Standard DTQW definition; the abstract names discrete-time quantum walks only.

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Walker at the center site with a symmetric spin state, prepared with H then S on the coin and X gates on the position register.
equations.justification: Chosen as the smallest instance; not stated in the abstract.

equations.label: Spin dephasing channel
equations.description: Per-step spin dephasing, implemented by an ancilla prepared with Ry(2 asin(sqrt(p_s))) and CZ or CX onto the coin, with the ancilla then discarded (fresh per step).
equations.abstract_quote: phenomenological model that distinguishes spin and spatial decoherence
equations.justification: A phase-flip channel is one plausible realization of spin decoherence; the exact form in the paper is unknown.
assumptions: Dephasing is Z-type and Markovian per step

equations.label: Spatial dephasing channel
equations.description: Per-step spatial dephasing using a fresh ancilla Ry(2 asin(sqrt(q))) controlling Z on the least significant position qubit. It damps coherences between sites of opposite parity by (1-2q) per step. Other position-bit choices, or Rz, give different spatial damping patterns.
equations.justification: A simple unitary-dilation toy model of spatial decoherence; the paper's form is not given.
assumptions: Only parity-resolving dephasing is modeled, a limited model of spatial decoherence

equations.label: Coherence length profile and Wigner function
equations.description: The coherence length is the width of C(d), for example the d at which C(d)/C(0) drops below 1/e. W is a discrete Wigner-type transform, computed classically. For even N, the half-integer subtlety is not handled.
equations.abstract_quote: We introduce the concept of coherence length in the discrete-time quantum walk, which quantifies the range of spatial coherences.
equations.justification: The abstract introduces a coherence length and a discrete Wigner function without formulas; these definitions are proposed.

registers.name: pos
registers.role: walker position, little-endian integer, qubit 0 is the least significant bit

registers.name: anc
registers.size: 2 per step (one spin, one spatial) if fresh per step
registers.role: environment for the dephasing dilation, traced out

specification.initial_state: pos set to N/2 by X on the top position qubit; coin in (|0>+i|1>)/sqrt2 via H then S.

steps.description: Prepare the initial state of eq_2.
For each step: apply H to the coin, then the conditional increment/decrement (MCX ripple, with the coin as control for increment and an X-conjugated coin for decrement).
After each shift, apply the spin dephasing dilation with a fresh ancilla (or for quasi-stationary dephasing a fixed Rz(theta_0) on the coin per run, averaged over runs).
Apply the spatial dephasing dilation with a fresh ancilla.
Obtain rho(x,x') from the statevector by tracing out the coin and ancillas, then compute C(d) and W(x,k) classically.

specification.measurement: Measure pos in the computational basis for P(x,T). Coherences come from the statevector or tomography, with no measurement in unitary or statevector tasks.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute P(x,T), its variance, C(d), the coherence length and W(x,k). Fit p_s and q by matching to simulated variance and shape. Average over sampled theta_0 for quasi-stationary dephasing.
assumptions: The abstract's experiment is modeled as a qubit-coin cyclic walk.
Ancillas are fresh per step, so the qubit count grows by 2T; keep T small to stay under the cap.
The walk length must be short enough to avoid wrap-around artifacts on the cyclic lattice.
missing_information: The paper's actual decoherence model and parameterization
The coin angle and initial state used experimentally
The qubit cap and query budget (no black box is involved here)
